evals.prompt: Use kis-op to reconcile issue 57 into the project and keep its lifecycle status current.
evals.expected_outcome: Uses repository/source evidence as authority, respects live Project schema, previews reconciliation, and does not invent unsupported fields.

assertions.text: Keeps repository issue/PR/Git evidence authoritative over the Project projection.
Uses preview-first idempotent reconciliation and reports truncated/incomplete inventory instead of fabricating absence.

human_review: Work Management semantics remain exact and non-duplicative.

evals.prompt: My KIS ChatGPT connection initializes but one capability is missing; diagnose the live KIS state and tell me whether MCP negotiation is involved.
evals.expected_outcome: Diagnoses KIS from live runtime evidence and composes mcp-development only when protocol interpretation is material.

assertions.text: Uses live initialization/capability/target evidence rather than assuming specification support equals runtime support.
Keeps generic MCP protocol interpretation in mcp-development instead of duplicating it in kis-mcp.

human_review: The answer separates KIS operation from MCP protocol design cleanly.

evals.prompt: Expose our KIS Skills catalogue through the emerging MCP Skills extension and let remote skills run their bundled scripts automatically.
evals.expected_outcome: Preserves the current read-only compatibility disposition, KIS catalogue authority, digest integrity, and explicit execution/permission boundaries.

assertions.text: Does not make the draft MCP Skills transport a second catalogue authority or production replacement.
Treats remote skill files as untrusted and refuses to infer script execution or permissions from skill metadata/digests.

human_review: Transport compatibility does not weaken KIS governance or security.
